author: The Infographics Show
description:
Quitting weed can feel surprisingly intense, especially after long-term or high-potency cannabis use.

This video explores what can happen to your body and brain after you stop using THC, from the first 12 hours through the following weeks. Withdrawal may bring anxiety, irritability, appetite changes, brain fog, vivid dreams, sleep disruption, and strong cravings as the body adjusts to functioning without regular cannabis. A major part of the process involves the endocannabinoid system and CB1 receptors, which help regulate mood, memory, stress, and sleep. Chronic THC exposure can reduce receptor availability, and research suggests those systems begin recovering after abstinence. Memory and learning may start improving within weeks, while sleep and emotional regulation can take longer to stabilize.

The first few days may be the hardest, but your brain doesn’t stay stuck there forever.
